name: Jürgen Klopp
scopeNote: Manager profile of Jürgen Klopp across three counted club spells: Mainz 05 (appointed 2001-02-27, first match 2001-02-28 v Duisburg; left 2008-06-30 after announcing in April 2008 he would not stay without promotion), Borussia Dortmund (2008-07-01 to 2015-06-30; last match the DFB-Pokal final 2015-05-30) and Liverpool (appointed 2015-10-08; last match 2024-05-19 v Wolves; Wikipedia's managerial record runs to 2024-05-31, used as the end date). Dates from English and German Wikipedia read at step 1. Mainz counts in full: Klopp's last game as a player was 2001-02-25, so he was never a player-manager, and the spell passes the 'known for' test on style (the Frank-derived pressing team) and on the move to a bigger job (Dortmund). Excluded: Red Bull Head of Global Soccer (2025-01-01 to 2026-07, not a coaching job) and the Germany national team (announced 2026-07-24, contract to 2030; 4 matches by 2026-10-04): too short and too new to be part of what he is known for. Style named by the evidence: 'Gegenpressing' (Spielverlagerung 2011: 'Gegenpressing direkt nach Ballverlust'; TFA 2020; Cox 2020) with fast vertical transitions; Klopp's own label is 'heavy metal' (AFP, 2013-11-05) and he calls the system 'organisiertes Chaos' (2026-09-23). Evolution: early Dortmund was a flat 4-4-1-1/4-4-2 (later 4-2-3-1) defending mostly from a mid-block and attacking on the counter after regains; Liverpool moved from a 4-2-3-1 (2015/16) to a 4-3-3 with attacking full-backs, a higher press and more possession and control from 2018/19 on (TFA 2020; PL Talking Tactics 2022; PL 2023). Marking: Klopp describes his career as built on ball-oriented zonal defending and rejects pitch-wide man-marking (2026); match analyses show man-oriented jumps by midfielders in the press (Spielverlagerung 2016; TFA 2022). Facts reused from the liverpool-2021-22 team file cite its original sources and its 2026-10-12 access date.

spellsCounted.reason: Recognisable pressing style inherited from Wolfgang Frank ('ausgeklügelte Pressing- und Gegenpressing-Taktik', bundesliga.com); first Bundesliga promotion in the club's history (2004) and two seasons kept up; led to the Dortmund job. Klopp stopped playing on appointment (last game as player 2001-02-25), so this is not a player-manager spell.
Bundesliga 2010/11 and 2011/12, DFB-Pokal 2012, Champions League final 2013; the Gegenpressing team with wide tactical coverage.
Champions League 2019, Premier League 2019/20, Club World Cup 2019, FA Cup 2022, EFL Cups 2022 and 2024; the evolved high-press 4-3-3.

spellsExcluded.reason: Executive role, not a coaching spell. Start date from Wikipedia; end month approximate (released when he took the Germany job, July 2026).

Announced 2026-07-24 (sport1.de), contract to 2030; Wikipedia lists the spell from 2026-08-15 with 4 matches by 2026-10-04. Far below the ~15-match minimum and no titles or tactical coverage yet: not part of what he is known for. His 2026-09-23 statements are kept in statedView.

openQuestions: Mainz counted in full by the 'known for' test (style plus move to Dortmund). FOOTBALL_RESEARCH.md cites 'Klopp's early player-manager years at Mainz' as an exclusion example, but Klopp stopped playing two days before his appointment (de.wikipedia), so there were no player-manager years. Confirm, or exclude 2001-04 (2. Bundesliga) if only the Bundesliga seasons should count.
Germany national team (announced 2026-07-24, 4 matches) is a new coaching spell not mentioned in the task; excluded as too short. Revisit once it has a body of work.

Marking (mar): Klopp's stated view (2026-09-23) is ball-oriented zonal defending ('ballorientiertes Verteidigen') instead of man-marking 'übers ganze Feld', and he says his 24-year career was built on it. Match analyses show man-oriented pressing by the midfield three (Spielverlagerung, Liverpool at Dortmund, 2016-04-07) and front three that 'man-mark tightly' while covering lanes (TFA 2022). Read as a zonal, ball-oriented base with man-oriented pressing jumps; confirm the weighting.

Mainz evidence is thin: only retrospective tier C (bundesliga.com, TFT 2020) and one 2011 Spielverlagerung line ('mutig auftretenden Mainzer'). No contemporary tactical analysis of Mainz 2001-08 was found; the style there is assumed to be Frank's zonal 4-4-2 pressing but that rests on Frank-era sources.

Style change inside the profile: heavy-metal counter-pressing and mid-block at Dortmund vs a higher press, more possession and attacking full-backs at Liverpool from 2018/19. Counted spells weigh the same; decide whether the audit should average them or lean on the later Liverpool side.

'Heavy metal': the earliest page read is the AFP wire of 2013-11-05 (Hürriyet Daily News) reporting an interview 'with English media' before Dortmund v Arsenal. The underlying English interview (likely a UK newspaper, early Nov 2013) was not found; if it is earlier, update the date.
The 'Gegenpressing is the best playmaker' quotes are taken from Cox's 2020 book extract, undated there; the original (probably Dortmund-era German interviews) was not found.
Search tool refused theathletic.com, 11freunde.de, dw.com, spiegel.de and zeit.de as domains, so German quality press on Mainz could not be searched.

sources.title: Aus der 2. Bundesliga an die Weltspitze: Die Story des Jürgen Klopp (bundesliga.com)
sources.evidence: Klopp's Mainz described as playing an "ausgeklügelte Pressing- und Gegenpressing-Taktik". On Wolfgang Frank: "Er hat uns die Laufwege eingehämmert. Für mich war das eine Offenbarung." Klopp (undated): "Wir konnten mit unserem System Spiele gewinnen gegen Mannschaften, die besser waren als wir." Promotion 2003/04 sealed by 3:0 v Trier. Page has no visible date (articleDate = access date; part of the '50 Jahre 2. Bundesliga' series, 2024). Retrospective, no period analysis.

sources.title: How Jürgen Klopp's focus on psychology has evolved Liverpool's players into "mentality monsters" (Dan Billingham, These Football Times)
sources.evidence: Paraphrase from the page: before the decisive May 2004 match v Eintracht Trier, Klopp hung a "Jaaaaaaaaa!" banner in the Mainz dressing room to lighten the mood; at promotion he publicly celebrated making the hard-working but limited Marco Rose a Bundesliga player. At Liverpool: kept pressure off in title races (Dec 2018 'enjoy the ride'; Feb 2019 "let's fasten the seatbelts and let go"); before the 2018 Kyiv final he gave his team talk in Ronaldo-branded boxer shorts to lower tension (Wijnaldum). Hired sports psychologist Lee Richardson (Nov 2019). The author credits his charisma with a young squad.

sources.title: Jürgen Klopp – Der Menschenfänger (Spielverlagerung.de)
sources.evidence: In 2010/11 BVB played "im 4-2-3-1-System"; the attacking three pushed "sehr weit in die Mitte". Earlier Mainz side called "mutig auftretenden Mainzer".

sources.title: Jürgen Klopp – Der Menschenfänger (Spielverlagerung.de)
sources.evidence: Defensive concept of "Gegenpressing direkt nach Ballverlust" and an "aggressive Ballrückgewinnungsstrategie"; offensive concept of "Schnelles vertikales Spiel nach Ballgewinn in Mittelfeld oder Angriff".

sources.title: Jürgen Klopp – Der Menschenfänger (Spielverlagerung.de)
sources.evidence: Centre-backs build up "ruhig" from the back; against deep opponents Sahin directs play. Preparation for 2010/11 focused "vor allem auf das Ballbesitzspiel" after critics said the team had "nach dem Ballgewinn keine Idee" (reader paraphrase around the quoted words).

sources.title: Jürgen Klopp – Der Menschenfänger (Spielverlagerung.de)
sources.evidence: The 2010/11 champions were "extrem jung": only Weidenfeller was older than 26; the Hummels-Subotić centre-back pair (Subotić 19 at the time) was called the "Kinderriegel". Klopp lets outstanding youth players train with the first team to show them a path into it.

sources.title: Jürgen Klopp – Der Menschenfänger (Spielverlagerung.de)
sources.evidence: Trusting relationships with all club staff are "die Grundlage seiner Arbeitsweise"; with the squad he is "autoritärer als gemeinhin angenommen" and handles "verschiedenen Persönlichkeiten unterschiedlich". Watzke: "So einen Menschenfänger habe ich noch nicht kennen gelernt." Klopp on assistant Buvač: "Fleisch gewordener Fußballsachverstand und Meister aller Trainingsformen" (undated).

sources.title: How Jürgen Klopp built an empire out of ruin at Borussia Dortmund (Will Sharp, These Football Times)
sources.evidence: 2008-11 recruitment: "the likes of Jakub Błaszczykowski and Robert Lewandowski were purchased for a pittance from Poland"; "Neven Subotić, Mats Hummels, Sven Bender, Kevin Großkreutz and Łukasz Piszczek were procured for similarly small sums from an assortment of German rivals"; Kagawa and Barrios imported, Götze promoted from the youth ranks. Style carried over from Mainz: quick transitions and "a culture built around gegenpressing", "an aggressive, exuberant, albeit exhausting, fast-paced system".

sources.title: Klopp: His tactical evolution from Dortmund to Liverpool (Max Bergmann, Total Football Analysis)
sources.evidence: Dortmund: "Watching back old games of his Dortmund side, one can often see them setting up in a mid-block." "In the following graphic, one can see them setting up in a compact 4-4-1-1 against Bayern." Liverpool: "At Liverpool, Klopp's pressing approach has become even more proactive." Dortmund seasons are not named; eventDate is an approximate early-Dortmund season.

sources.title: Klopp: His tactical evolution from Dortmund to Liverpool (Max Bergmann, Total Football Analysis)
sources.evidence: Dortmund triggers: "A bad pass, miscontrol of the ball or a closed body shape of a receiving player"; "If the opposition played backwards to reset their attack, Dortmund would not necessarily continue their press though"; "The two forward players were especially supposed to use their cover-shadows to prevent passes into midfield" (zonal, lane-blocking). Liverpool: "as Liverpool press higher than Dortmund, horizontal passes are also used as a pressing trigger." No explicit zonal/man label. Dortmund seasons not named.

sources.title: Klopp: His tactical evolution from Dortmund to Liverpool (Max Bergmann, Total Football Analysis)
sources.evidence: Liverpool: "Since their opponents are often satisfied with a goalless draw, Liverpool need to be more patient in possession." "The aim has drifted towards the prevention of counter-attacks and the increase of possession." "they are not offered as many counter-attacking opportunities after their 'Gegenpressing' as during Klopp's time at Dortmund."

sources.title: Klopp: His tactical evolution from Dortmund to Liverpool (Max Bergmann, Total Football Analysis)
sources.evidence: Dortmund: "Dortmund would often build up their play through one side of the pitch"; "the wingers tucked inside quite early attacking down the half-spaces." Liverpool: "He wants both of his full-backs, Andy Robertson and Trent Alexander-Arnold to attack high up the pitch"; "Right-back Alexander-Arnold sent in an impressive total of 313 crosses in 2019/20 so far."

sources.title: Klopp: His tactical evolution from Dortmund to Liverpool (Max Bergmann, Total Football Analysis)
sources.evidence: "While he deployed Robert Lewandowski as a rather classic number nine at Dortmund, he banks on Roberto Firmino as a false nine at Liverpool." Van Dijk: "Besides playing short combination play with his good technique, Van Dijk can play long diagonal balls with precision."

sources.title: Klopp: His tactical evolution from Dortmund to Liverpool (Max Bergmann, Total Football Analysis)
sources.evidence: Conclusion: "he also improved his set-piece strategies with the help of external coaches such as a throw-in coach." Liverpool era.

sources.title: Why Jürgen Klopp's gegenpressing with Dortmund was revolutionary (Michael Cox, Zonal Marking extract, Sky Sports)
sources.evidence: Dortmund "piled players into the immediate vicinity of the player in possession"; often a medium block "standing off the opposition centre-backs", pressing once the ball reached full-backs or midfielders, rarely a full-pitch press (reader paraphrase). Wide midfielders Großkreutz and Błaszczykowski tucked inside to compress. Running target: "If they covered more than 118km collectively in nine out of ten matches" they got extra winter-break days. Season not named; eventDate approximate.

sources.title: Borussia Dortmund – Liverpool 1:1 (Spielverlagerung.com)
sources.evidence: Marking (one match, Europa League QF first leg): Liverpool pressed "between a 4-3-3 and a 4-5-1" in a "horizontally-compact 4-3-3 structure"; "The three in midfield were rather man-oriented in their pressing"; "The two English midfielders were energetic without possession and followed Castro and Mkhitaryan quite closely." "When acting deeper in a 4-5-1 shape, Liverpool's pressing was much weaker." Klopp "elected for more of a counter-attacking strategy to the game."

sources.title: Borussia Dortmund – Liverpool 1:1 (Spielverlagerung.com)
sources.evidence: Away at his former club Klopp "elected for more of a counter-attacking strategy to the game"; Liverpool "created good chances from quick direct attacks and set pieces". One match.

sources.title: PL30: How Klopp transformed Liverpool into champions (Adrian Clarke, Talking Tactics)
sources.evidence: "During his first campaign, Klopp used a 4-2-3-1 system" (2015/16); Mané (2016) and Salah (2017) moved Liverpool to a 4-3-3. Pressing: "In 2015/16, Liverpool pressed ferociously, winning possession inside the final third five times per match"; 2019/20 "Liverpool topped the Premier League rankings, winning the ball back 6.7 times per 90 minutes inside the final third." Fast-break goals rose from 1 (2015/16) to 9 (2017/18 and 2019/20, 1st). Replacing Clyne and Moreno with Alexander-Arnold and Robertson "was a real turning point"; open-play crosses per 90 rose from 12.8 to 18.0 (2018/19 to 2019/20).

sources.title: PL30: How Klopp transformed Liverpool into champions (Adrian Clarke, Talking Tactics)
sources.evidence: Fast-break goals by season (total, PL rank): 2015/16 1 (12th), 2016/17 2 (10th), 2017/18 9 (1st), 2018/19 6 (3rd), 2019/20 9 (1st). Defence: 92 goals conceded in the first two seasons, 21 in 2019/20; "The presence of a dominant goalkeeper in Alisson and imposing centre-back in Van Dijk made a monumental difference."

sources.title: How Guardiola and Klopp's tactics have continuously evolved (Alex Keble, Premier League)
sources.evidence: Klopp's arrival-era football called "heavy-metal Germanic football" with "straight-lined transitions" and "full-throttle pressing"; now he "has never been so committed to controlling possession." Opponent-specific plans against City: Oct 2021 "an unexpected tactic of hitting longer balls over the top of the Man City defence"; Oct 2022 (1-0) Liverpool sat "their defensive line much deeper"; Apr 2023 a "wild 4-2-4 formation". Column.

sources.title: Jürgen Klopp hails 'unbelievable' Liverpool youngsters after Carabao Cup final win over Chelsea (TNT Sports / Eurosport)
sources.evidence: With a long injury list, academy graduates Bobby Clark, James McConnell, Jayden Danns and Jarell Quansah came off the bench and Conor Bradley (20) started in the 1-0 EFL Cup final win. Klopp: "A team, a squad, an academy full of character." "We thought we needed fresh legs - and the fresh legs were fresh, but very young. But they did the jobs." Forced by injuries, not a planned youth policy.

sources.title: Jurgen Klopp – Liverpool – Tactical Analysis (2021-22 Edition) (TheMastermindSite) [reused from liverpool-2021-22]
sources.evidence: Read in the liverpool-2021-22 run: Alisson sweeps up "any messes on the heels of the team's high line" and can go long when pressed; build-up between a diamond and a 2-5-3 or 3+1, Fabinho in front of the centre-backs, Alexander-Arnold often part of a back three (paraphrase). "the Reds have played all 22 matches this season in their favoured 4-3-3 shape". Set pieces: 12 set-piece goals, throw-in coach Thomas Grønnemark (paraphrase).

sources.title: Liverpool 2021/22: The key factors behind Liverpool's impressive defensive record (Total Football Analysis) [reused from liverpool-2021-22]
sources.evidence: Read in the liverpool-2021-22 run: Van Dijk: "We want to keep a high line because we know we can win the ball up high, and it's the risk you have to take"; 140 offsides provoked. Marking in the press: "They man-mark tightly, ready to pounce like sharks, while also covering passing lanes and out-balls"; "The front three, who are responsible to defend five or sometimes six players."

sources.title: Liverpool's unsung heroes proving their worth (Premier League) [reused from liverpool-2021-22]
sources.evidence: Read in the liverpool-2021-22 run: Klopp the only manager "to have used the same formation in all 38 matches this season" (4-3-3); "Liverpool's strength in numbers allowed Klopp to influence the course of matches through his second-half changes."

sources.title: Alexander-Arnold, Robertson and Alisson added to Liverpool's leadership group (Goal) [reused from liverpool-2021-22]
sources.evidence: Read in the liverpool-2021-22 run: players' committee chosen by a dressing-room vote. Klopp: "We had the three who stayed, and then the players voted for another three."

sources.title: Jürgen Klopp – Wikipedia
sources.evidence: Jonathan Wilson: "a hugely charismatic figure who inspires players with his personality"; LMA chief executive said Klopp "redefined man-management"; Firmino: "He motivates us in a different way every day." Assistant Željko Buvač (2001-2018) nicknamed "the brain", reportedly left after taking issue with Pepijn Lijnders' growing influence. At Liverpool he "developed his tactics to incorporate more possession based football". Quotes undated; eventDate approximate. Read characters 0-200000 of 210185.

statedView.quote: It's like an orchestra, but they play a silent song. I like heavy metal, I always want it to be loud.
statedView.note: AFP wire, Dortmund, 2013-11-05, reporting an interview with English media before Dortmund v Arsenal (CL group F, 2013-11-06). Earliest dated appearance read; the underlying English interview was not found. Arsenal = 'orchestra', his own football = 'heavy metal'.

statedView.quote: Arsenal have a philosophy from Arsene Wenger, I love that, but I can't coach that way, I am different.
Gegenpressing lets you win back the ball nearer to the goal.
statedView.note: Undated in Cox's book extract; Dortmund era. Original interview not found.

statedView.quote: No playmaker in the world can be as good as a good gegenpressing situation.

statedView.quote: Wir konnten mit unserem System Spiele gewinnen gegen Mannschaften, die besser waren als wir.
statedView.note: About Mainz under Frank and himself. Undated on the page.

Wir haben das in meinen Vereinen ‚organisiertes Chaos' genannt. Für andere sah es chaotisch aus, für uns war es organisiert.

statedView.quote: Ballorientiertes Verteidigen ist nicht kompliziert. Das werden wir organisieren.
statedView.note: Marking: the article says he prefers ball-oriented defending to 'Manndeckung übers ganze Feld' (Kompany's Bayern), learnt under Frank when 'die Raumdeckung, eingeführt wurde' ('Ein Erweckungserlebnis'), and that he built 'eine 24-jährige Trainerkarriere' on it. Also: 'dass alle immer verantwortlich sind für die Defensive. ALLE IMMER!' and 'Das Defensivverhalten ist das Trampolin und das Fangnetz.'

influences.note: His coach at Mainz, who introduced zonal marking and a back four there; Klopp calls it 'eine Offenbarung' and an 'Erweckungserlebnis' (bundesliga.com; leinetal24, 2026-09-23).
Frank's model; Klopp recalls watching Sacchi's defensive-drill video '500 times' (Guardian interview, seen only in a reader comment on Spielverlagerung.de and in a search summary; not verified).

confidence.reason: Dortmund and Liverpool are well covered by tier A-B sources that agree (Spielverlagerung 2011 and 2016, TFA 2020 and 2022, TheMastermindSite 2022, Premier League Talking Tactics 2022) on Gegenpressing, fast vertical transitions and the shift to a higher press, 4-3-3 and more possession at Liverpool. Kept at medium because Mainz, a counted spell of equal weight, rests only on retrospective tier C pieces; several Dortmund facts are retrospective without exact seasons; marking is mixed (stated zonal ball-oriented base vs man-oriented pressing in match analyses); and the gegenpressing quotes are undated.
